big: Rohan sees his ₹5 lakh portfolio fall 20% to ₹4 lakh. He feels the ₹1 lakh loss sharply. If it had risen ₹1 lakh instead, he would have felt happy, but not nearly as strongly. Losses hurt more than gains please.

lines: I know it is a paper loss, but I cannot sleep. Should I sell?
That feeling is normal. People feel a loss more strongly than an equal gain. But a fall on paper becomes a real loss only if you sell. Decide with a plan, not with the pain.

small: needed to recover from a 20% fall
alt: Bars showing a portfolio falling from one hundred to eighty and needing a rise of twenty five percent to return to one hundred
caps: To get back to 100 it needs to rise by 20, which is 25% of 80.
Falls need a bigger rise to recover. That is why they scare us.

rows: A fall looks small in ten years of data
A paper loss is a real loss only if you sell
note: These habits help with fear. They do not remove risk, so choose an amount you can hold through a fall.

q: Meena's portfolio falls 10%. She wants to sell at once to stop the pain. What is the better step?
opts: Pause, and follow the agreed plan
Sell everything that she holds today
why: A rule agreed earlier helps her act on facts and not on fear.
Selling in a panic can lock in the loss.
Checking hourly adds to the pain and the urge to sell.
Borrowing to invest adds risk when she is already anxious.

q: A ₹4 lakh portfolio has fallen from ₹5 lakh. When does the ₹1 lakh become a real loss?
opts: Only on the day it fell
On the first of every month
why: The loss is on paper until he sells, even on the day of the fall.
If he sells at the low price, it does become real.
A fall on paper becomes a real loss only if he sells.
Calendar dates do not turn a paper loss into a real one.

q: A portfolio falls 20%. How much must it rise from there to get back to its start?
why: A 20% rise on 80 reaches only 96 in all.
From 80 to 100 is a rise of 20, or 25% of 80.
A 10% rise on 80 reaches only 88 in all.
A 15% rise on 80 reaches only 92 in all.

q: Which habit helps reduce the urge to sell in a fall?
opts: Watching the price every single minute
Viewing a long chart, checking less
why: Watching every minute only feeds the fear and the urge.
Scary headlines raise the urge to sell for no reason.
Friends who sold may be reacting to fear too.
A long chart shows a fall in context, and fewer checks calm.

pts: Losses hurt more than equal gains please.
A fall is a real loss only if you sell.
A 20% fall needs a 25% rise to recover. Agree a rule before a fall.
